projects.title: Augmum
paragraphs: • Project overview: Augmum is a robotics R&D project exploring how observed human hand movements can be learned and reproduced by a robotic arm with minimal direct operator control.

• Engineering challenge: The problem required several disciplines to work together — visual perception, machine learning, motion interpretation, robotics middleware, and physical actuation — so that human movement could be converted into useful robot behaviour.

• My contribution: Worked on the machine-learning and computer-vision side of the system and supported integration with the ROS-based robotics stack using C++, Python, TensorFlow, and related AI techniques.

• Technical approach: Explored neural-network and CNN-based methods, YOLO-based vision, reinforcement-learning concepts, and ROS integration to connect perception outputs with downstream robot actions.

• Professional value: The project gave me practical experience at the intersection of AI and robotics, particularly the challenge of taking perception and learning techniques beyond experimentation and connecting them to a physical robotic system.

projects.title: KenOB1
paragraphs: • Project overview: Contributed to RoboGuard KenOB1, a human-sized autonomous security robot developed by Oneberry Technologies in Singapore, with a focus on improving its perception, localisation, and autonomous-navigation capability.

• Engineering challenge: The existing platform relied on 2D SICK LiDAR. Expanding the sensing stack to 3D LiDAR and depth cameras required the new hardware to work reliably with the robot’s existing ROS-based localisation, mapping, navigation, and motion-control components.
• My contribution: Upgraded the sensing configuration to include a Velodyne VLP-16 and depth cameras, and worked on integrating the new perception hardware into the autonomy stack.
• Technical approach: Worked with ROS, C/Python, RTAB-Map, HDL Graph SLAM, TEB Local Planner, Intel RealSense D435i, ZED Mini, Velodyne LiDAR, and Roboteq motor-control hardware.

• Outcome: The work broadened the robot’s environmental perception and extended the autonomy stack beyond the original 2D sensing setup, while giving me hands-on experience integrating sensors, SLAM, localisation, planning, and mobile-robot hardware as one operational system.

projects.title: Sidewalk Robot
paragraphs: • Project overview: Developed an autonomous mobile-robot prototype at Oneberry Technologies for camera-based navigation along pedestrian sidewalks.

• Engineering challenge: The robot needed to distinguish traversable sidewalk from surrounding areas using live visual input, remain aligned with the path, and react to obstacles without relying on a fully predefined route.
• My contribution: Developed the perception workflow used to identify free space and connected that perception output with the robot’s navigation and motion-control pipeline.

• Technical approach: Used semantic segmentation, OpenCV, Isaac SDK, ROS, ROS Bridge, C/C++, ZED/USB camera input, and Sabertooth motor control to support path detection, path following, and obstacle avoidance.

• Professional value: The project strengthened my understanding of end-to-end autonomous navigation by connecting computer-vision inference with middleware and physical robot movement rather than treating perception as an isolated software task.

projects.title: Evolutionary Flocking Shooter
paragraphs: • Project overview: Built an AI-driven simulation in Unity3D and C# for postgraduate coursework, using evolutionary computation to train enemy agents instead of defining their behaviour entirely through scripted rules.

• Engineering challenge: The agents needed to discover useful behaviour over successive generations, including locating the target, avoiding the tower’s attack zone, and improving their ability to approach and destroy the objective.
• My contribution: Designed and implemented the simulation environment, agent behaviour, fitness evaluation, and genetic-algorithm cycle used to evolve each new generation.
• Technical approach: Used a Genetic Algorithm within Unity3D to evaluate agent performance, select stronger behaviours, and progressively improve decision-making across generations.

• Outcome: By approximately the seventh generation, the agents demonstrated the intended behaviours of locating the objective, avoiding the defended region, and attacking the target. I completed the project in around 20 days and achieved a 92% module mark.

projects.title: Fusion Fission Dynamics
paragraphs: • Project overview: Developed artificial-life and swarm-robotics experiments using Thymio robots and NetLogo as part of postgraduate coursework in Artificial Life with Robotics.
• Engineering challenge: The objective was to create coordinated group behaviour from local sensing and simple individual rules rather than relying on centralised control.

• My contribution: Implemented behaviours for following, flocking, obstacle detection, and line avoidance, and designed multiple sensing regions that influenced how each robot reacted to nearby robots and environmental features.

• Technical approach: Divided perception into far-sight, near-sight, and perspective zones, then varied their parameters to observe how sensing range and spatial context changed individual decisions and group formation.
• Professional value: The project provided practical experience with emergent behaviour, distributed decision-making, and the relationship between local perception rules and swarm-level dynamics.

projects.title: Super Nim
paragraphs: • Project overview: Developed Super Nim in Python for an MSc Artificial Intelligence module, extending the traditional mathematical game of Nim with additional actions and a larger decision space.
• Engineering challenge: The custom split, merge, and Collatz-Ulam operations created more possible future states than standard Nim, requiring the AI player to evaluate alternatives efficiently.
• My contribution: Designed the game rules and implemented the complete playable application, including support for human players, computer-controlled players, and AI decision-making.
• Technical approach: Implemented a Minimax-based AI player with alpha-beta pruning to reduce unnecessary search branches while preserving the quality of move selection.

• Professional value: The project demonstrates practical application of adversarial search, state modelling, algorithmic optimisation, and AI decision-making in a complete interactive program. The project was completed in approximately 12 days.

projects.title: Snake and Cake
paragraphs: • Project overview: Developed Snake and Cake, a desktop game in C++ and OpenGL for a university Computer Graphics project, inspired by classic Nokia-era snake games.
• My contribution: Implemented the core gameplay loop, player controls, rendering behaviour, difficulty progression, and application state management.
• Technical approach: Used object-oriented C++ to organise the game logic and OpenGL for real-time rendering and visual updates.
• Features delivered: Implemented selectable difficulty levels together with start, pause, resume, and stop behaviour to create a complete playable desktop application.
• Professional value: The project provided early hands-on experience with real-time application structure, graphics programming, user input, and object-oriented software design.

projects.title: Chefu
paragraphs: • Project overview: Developed Chefu as a web and mobile-oriented marketplace concept designed to connect customers with nearby chefs while giving chefs a platform to present and sell their services.
• Product scope: The application supported chef profiles and portfolios, customer ratings and reviews, recipe sales, and location-aware functionality for booked services.
• My contribution: Worked across the application stack, implementing server-side functionality, data-driven pages, user interactions, and workflows connecting customers with service providers.

• Technical approach: Built the application with PHP and CodeIgniter on the backend, supported by JavaScript, jQuery, AJAX, Bootstrap, HTML, and CSS for responsive and interactive client-side behaviour.

• Professional value: The project demonstrates end-to-end web-application development across business logic, user-facing workflows, asynchronous interactions, and integration between backend and frontend components.
